title: India Eye Series Seal As Wellington Wind Tests Bowlers In Third T20I
excerpt: Leading 2-0 after two Christchurch wins, India can close out the five-match series on Tuesday — if they handle Hnry Stadium's 55 kph gusts, short square boundaries and New Zealand's spinners.
body:
• India lead the five-match T20I series 2-0 after two four-wicket wins in Christchurch and can seal the series in Wellington on Tuesday, October 27.
  • The third T20I at Hnry Stadium starts at 8:00 PM local time (12:30 PM IST), with square boundaries of around 60 metres and wind expected to shape tactics.
  • Swirling winds of up to 55 kph swept Wellington on match eve, and bowling coach Morne Morkel wants India to treat the wind as a challenge, not an excuse.
  • New Zealand must win without Matt Henry and Lockie Ferguson, while Ishan Kishan remains out for India and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi keeps the No. 3 spot.

India arrive in Wellington with the T20I series in their grasp. Two wins from two in Christchurch have put Shreyas Iyer's side 2-0 up in the five-match series against New Zealand, and one more win in the third T20I on Tuesday, October 27 would close out the series with two games to spare. The match is at Hnry Stadium, starting at 8:00 PM local time (12:30 PM IST), per the Cricbuzz preview.

The recent record backs the visitors. Including the T20 World Cup final in March, India have won 18 of their 21 T20Is against New Zealand this decade, and nine of their last ten meetings overall. New Zealand have lost their last two home series against India.

Why Wellington is a different test

Wellington asks harder questions than Christchurch. The square boundaries at Hnry Stadium are shorter, at around 60 metres, but the wind is the variable neither side can fully plan for. Cricbuzz reports swirling winds of up to 55 kph on match eve, expected to ease slightly by match day but still a factor, with some rain forecast on Tuesday that should clear before the start.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2114522397713760447

India have been caught out by these conditions before. They lost 2-0 in Ireland earlier this year in bouncier, windier conditions, a tour Cricbuzz notes came during Iyer's first stint as captain, when the breeze and the bounce proved difficult to negotiate. The ESPNcricinfo preview makes the same point: India are still missing Jasprit Bumrah and Hardik Pandya, had only one training session before the first game, and have won through better execution of bowling plans that will now need adjusting for Wellington's dimensions.

"You're either going to see it as a challenge or you're going to see it as a negative or it's going to let you down. And hopefully we can get those guys in the mental space where they look forward to that challenge" — Morne Morkel on the Wellington wind

Where the game will be decided

Morkel has set the terms for the rest of the tour. After allowing for travel, jet lag and limited training in the opening games, he wants standards to rise from here, starting with the bowling and with batting against spin. The numbers explain the second point. New Zealand's spinners have taken eight wickets at an economy of 8.25 in this series, while their pacers have taken four wickets at 11.78. Mitchell Santner and Michael Bracewell have bowled 16 overs between them for 132 runs and eight wickets, and India's middle order has largely held back against them — Tilak Varma, for example, has scored at a strike rate of 76 against spin and 220 against pace in the series.

New Zealand coach Rob Walter put his side's problem plainly: "I felt we've played pretty well in probably 80% of each game. We just haven't been able to put the finishing touches on it each time, which is disappointing." The hosts have also been hit in the pace department. Matt Henry, who bowled only two overs on Saturday, has been rested for the remainder of the series, and Lockie Ferguson misses this match, leaving Kyle Jamieson, Adam Milne and Jacob Duffy to lead the attack.

Team news and what comes next

India are expected to stay with the balance that won in Christchurch. With Ishan Kishan out for at least one more game, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi should get another innings at No. 3. Cricbuzz lists India's probable XI as Sanju Samson, Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Shreyas Iyer, Tilak Varma, Naman Dhir, Nitish Reddy, Axar Patel, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Arshdeep Singh and Prince Yadav. New Zealand's probable XI is Finn Allen, Tim Seifert, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Bevon Jacobs, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner, Nathan Smith, Kyle Jamieson, Adam Milne and Jacob Duffy.

History offers the hosts little comfort: New Zealand have won only two of their seven T20Is at Hnry Stadium since 2020. Win on Tuesday and India take an unassailable 3-0 lead. Lose, and New Zealand keep the series alive — but only if they finally turn 80 percent of a good performance into a complete one, in the wind.
